answer.evidence: The brown box has a light 1-row front rim line at row 13 (L=197). Above it, rows 2-12 show a mounded heap of grey ore with gold flecks, and the silhouette widens from 2 to 26 px over rows 2-7. This is contents visible inside an open container (d). Below the rim, rows 14-24 are the brown front face, 11 rows tall, with a dark base line at row 24. Two small wheels sit at rows 25-30. No receding side face is drawn. The heap is read as contents rather than a rim, so the main top surface is about 11 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ore cart is a small prop. Measured: 15 visible tones per tile is close to the stall (17) and well (20) and above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 25%, higher than every reference (0-13%), so some flat areas remain, probably on the cart body. 95% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is a uniform near-black/grey line. The references with comparable structure (well, stall, hedge) have tinted dark-material outlines at 0-33% neutral. By eye, the ore pile has a few grey tones and the cart body is a brown-grey wood with metal bands, but it has fewer ramp steps (about 4) than the 5-6 on the references. The wheels and body read as sticker-like, outlined in neutral dark. The outline and the flat coverage are shallower than the Beodeul standard, so it fails.
